questions.explanation: Velocity includes both magnitude and direction, so changing direction means velocity changes even if speed stays the same.

questions.definition: The rate of change of velocity.
questions.clue: Measured in metres per second squared.
questions.explanation: Acceleration occurs when an object speeds up, slows down, or changes direction.

questions.definition: The single overall force acting on an object after all forces are combined.
questions.explanation: If the resultant force is not zero, an object will accelerate in the direction of that force.

questions.definition: The product of mass and velocity.
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved in a closed system, which is useful when analysing collisions.

questions.clue: Calculated using density = mass divided by volume.
questions.explanation: Density tells us how much mass is packed into a given volume and is measured in kg/m3 or g/cm3.

questions.clue: Calculated using pressure = force divided by area.
questions.explanation: A smaller area produces greater pressure for the same force, such as a sharp knife cutting more easily.

questions.definition: The rate of flow of electric charge.
questions.explanation: Current is the amount of charge passing a point each second. It is measured with an ammeter.

questions.definition: The energy transferred per unit charge.
questions.explanation: Voltage is measured in volts and provides the push that drives charge around a circuit.

questions.definition: A measure of how difficult it is for current to flow through a component.
questions.explanation: Resistance depends on the material and dimensions of a conductor and can change with temperature.

questions.definition: The distance from one point on a wave to the same point on the next wave.
questions.clue: Crest to crest is one example.
questions.explanation: Wavelength is measured in metres and is related to wave speed and frequency.

questions.definition: The number of waves passing a point each second.
questions.explanation: Frequency is measured in Hz. Higher frequency sound waves have a higher pitch.

questions.definition: The time taken for half the unstable nuclei in a radioactive sample to decay.
questions.explanation: Half-life is constant for a particular isotope and helps predict how activity changes over time.
